data.title: MDQ Specification Audit: multiple-choice
data.scope: The `multiple-choice` question type: `docs/question-types/multiple-choice.md`, `schema/multiple-choice.yaml`, its grammar, and the shared specs it depends on (`docs/references/grammar.md`, `docs/references/patterns.md`, `docs/question-types/question-base.md`, `docs/exam.md`, `docs/responses.md`).

data.title: Contradictions
Ambiguities
Omissions
Inconsistencies
Grammar violations
Schema mismatches

data.methodology:
Automated checks: `uv run scripts/spec_audit.py` passed all 14 steps before the audit (schema bundle, docs, Additional Rules, lint codes, valid and invalid corpus, frontmatter tables, property consistency, code blocks, schema agreement).

Manual review: the lead auditor read the shared specs and the multiple-choice spec and recorded contradictions, ambiguities, omissions and inconsistencies. A grammar subagent turned the multiple-choice grammar and the shared grammar into Lark grammars and tested what they accept and reject against the stated rules. A second, independent subagent reviewed the multiple-choice spec against `schema/multiple-choice.yaml`, ran every complete example through `mdq validate`, and checked the Additional Rules table against the MUST/SHOULD/MAY statements of the text.

data.title: Symmetric grading has no formula for the unspecified score
data.snippet:
* **symmetric** (default): Unspecified scores are computed in such a way that
  the average score of randomly picking choices is zero. This depends on the
  number of choices and the number of choices with specified scores. The value
  derived this way is clamped to the range `[-1, 0]`.
data.description: The rule is stated only as a goal (the mean of a uniform random pick is zero). The formula `u = -(sum of specified scores) / (number of unspecified choices)`, then clamped to [-1, 0], must be reverse-engineered from the table at lines 209-216. The text does not say that the random pick is uniform, nor that an explicit `[0%]` counts as specified, and no table row has an explicit 0.
data.impact: Two implementations can derive different scores, for example when `[0%]` is present or when the clamp applies, and the spec gives no single equation to test them against.
data.fix: State the formula explicitly, say that `[0%]` counts as specified, and add a table row such as `[1, 0, _, _]` (-0.5).

data.title: duplicate-choice-text does not say how texts are compared
data.snippet: The choice text MUST NOT be empty. And all choice texts MUST be unique.
data.description: The spec separates exact duplicates (critical `duplicate-choice-text`) from visually identical texts (info `visually-identical-choices`) and uses `foo bar` vs `foo  bar` as an example of visual equivalence. It does not say whether uniqueness is checked on the source text, on whitespace-normalized text, or after rendering. mdq-py reports `foo bar` / `foo  bar` as `duplicate-choice-text` (critical), which the example at lines 94-101 presents as the info-level case.
data.impact: The same pair of choices is a hard error in one implementation and a hint in another; question-base also lets implementations normalize whitespace in strings, so the result depends on that choice.
data.fix: Define the comparison for `duplicate-choice-text` (for example: after collapsing runs of `ws` and `nl` to one space and trimming) and move `foo bar` / `foo  bar` to that rule, or say that it compares the source text verbatim.
data.conditions: Verified with `mdq validate` on a list with `* [*] foo bar` and `* [ ] foo  bar`.

data.title: "Marked" refers both to the answer key and to the student's pick
data.snippet: strategy is ignored if the marked choice defines a score, and the question is
data.description: Line 6 and line 106 use "mark" for the author marking a choice correct (`[*]`). The Grading section uses "the marked choice" and "marking a choice with an omitted score" for the choice the student picked. A reader can take line 191 as "if the choice marked `[*]` defines a score".
data.impact: The central rule of the Grading section can be misread.
data.fix: Use "picked" (as the Feedback section does) for the student's choice, and keep "mark" for the author.

data.title: Grammar of an item forbids what the prose of the item allows, and the reverse
data.snippet: item          : ws? "[" value "]" ws? (choice_id ws?)? md_inline+ nl extra_lines? (feedback? comments? | comments feedback)
data.description: The prose says each feedback or comment line is "preceded by their corresponding punctuation", but `feedback_line` and `comment_line` accept unmarked `extra_lines` after them. The grammar forbids interleaving (`> a`, `! b`, `> c`), but the prose never says so and no lint code covers it; mdq-py accepts that item and joins the two feedback lines into `a c`.
data.impact: Authors and implementations cannot tell whether a lazy continuation line or an interleaved block is valid, and an interleaved item is silently reordered.
data.fix: Align with patterns.md "Pattern items": state that unmarked lines continue the previous part, that feedback and comment MUST NOT interleave, and give the error code for an interleaved item.
data.conditions: Verified with `mdq validate` and `mdq show` on an item with `> a`, `! b`, `> c`.

data.title: No mapping from a choice item to its AST object
data.snippet: Each choice may represent additional information besides its text.
data.description: The spec defines how `value` maps to `score` (lines 112-116), but not how the rest of the item maps to `text`, `id`, `feedback` and `comment`: how lines of a multi-line text, feedback or comment are joined, whether `>`/`!` and the following `ws` are stripped, what a blank line inside an item does, and what happens with block content in an item (a second paragraph, a nested list, a code block). mdq-py appends a second paragraph of the item to the feedback. patterns.md defines these rules for pattern items, but multiple-choice.md does not refer to them.
data.impact: The JSON/YAML form of the same markdown can differ between implementations; the round trip markdown -> AST -> markdown is undefined.
data.fix: Add a "Markdown to AST mapping" subsection for choices, reusing the continuation-line rules of patterns.md, and state that block content other than the item lines is an error (with a code) or define where it goes.
data.conditions: Verified with `mdq show` on an item followed by a blank line and an indented paragraph.

data.title: An item with only a choice id has two readings
data.snippet: A `choice_id` is a `SLUG` between square brackets, right after the value. A
data.description: For `* [*] [brasilia]`, the grammar (`(choice_id ws?)? md_inline+`) only parses `[brasilia]` as the choice text, since `md_inline+` cannot be empty. The prose says a bracket with a SLUG right after the value is a choice id, which leaves an empty text. mdq-py follows the prose and reports `blank-choice-text`.
data.impact: A grammar-driven implementation accepts a document that the reference implementation rejects.
data.fix: State that a SLUG bracket after the value is always the id, so an item with nothing after it has an empty text (`blank-choice-text`); make the grammar match.

data.title: Severity of a blank choice text disagrees with question-base
data.snippet: | choices[].text     | critical | blank-choice-text                    | must not be empty                                         |
data.description: question-base says a whitespace-only string in a text field other than preamble/epilogue/stem is the `blank-text-field` warning, and lists "choice text" among the text fields. multiple-choice makes a blank choice text a critical `blank-choice-text`. The rule text "must not be empty" also repeats the schema `minLength: 1` instead of describing the blank case that the code checks.
data.impact: A reader of question-base expects a warning; the type spec and mdq-py give an error.
data.fix: In question-base, exclude choice text (and other per-type blank codes) from the `blank-text-field` sentence; reword the rule as "must have at least one visible character".

data.title: Lint codes for correct choices are named differently across choice types
data.snippet: | choices[].score    | info     | multiple-choice-no-correct-choice    | at least one choice should have a score of 1              |
data.description: multiple-selection uses `no-correct-choice`; multiple-choice uses `multiple-choice-no-correct-choice` and `multiple-choice-many-correct-choices`, but the unprefixed `all-choices-correct`. "Correct" means `score == 1` here and `correct: true` in multiple-selection; `all-choices-correct` does not restate which.
data.impact: Users filtering or disabling lint codes must learn per-type spellings for the same check.
data.fix: Either drop the `multiple-choice-` prefix (share `no-correct-choice`) or prefix all type-specific codes; define "correct" as `score == 1` in the rule text.

data.title: all-or-nothing does not mean all-or-nothing in multiple choice
data.snippet: * **all-or-nothing**: Unspecified scores are treated as 0[^2].
data.description: A pick of a `[50%]` choice scores 0.5 under `all-or-nothing`, because a specified score overrides the strategy. In multiple-selection and true-false the strategy forbids partial credit. The footnote only says it equals `partial`.
data.impact: An exam that sets `grading: all-or-nothing` expecting no partial credit still gives partial credit on multiple-choice questions with percentage values.
data.fix: Say explicitly that percentage values still give partial credit under `all-or-nothing`, or make `all-or-nothing` round non-1 scores down to 0.

data.title: Body syntax uses "comments", the schema field is `comment`
data.snippet: comments      : comment_line+
data.description: The grammar and prose call the `!` block "comments"; the AST field is the singular `comment`, and the spec never states the link.
data.impact: Minor: a reader looks for a `comments` field.
data.fix: Use "comment" in the grammar and prose, or state that the `!` lines map to `comment`.

data.title: Normative text cites an mdq-py function
data.snippet: the text content when it needs an addressable document (e.g., mdq-py:
data.description: The spec refers to `with_ids()` of mdq-py. The spec is language-neutral elsewhere.
data.impact: The spec becomes stale when the API is renamed.
data.fix: Refer to the addressability section of responses.md instead.

data.text: The `score` range, the `choices` minimum, the `id` SLUG pattern, and the `grading`/`shuffle` enums and `inherit` defaults agree between multiple-choice.md and schema/multiple-choice.yaml.
The `grading` and `shuffle` inheritance rules agree between multiple-choice.md, exam.md and the schema descriptions (`inherit` default, `symmetric`/`false` outside an exam).
The six rows of the grading table match the formula u = clamp(-Σspecified / #unspecified, -1, 0), including both clamp cases.

data.title: extra_lines absorbs feedback and comment lines, so the item grammar is ambiguous
data.snippet: extra_lines   : (md_inline* nl)+
data.description:
`md_inline` is any inline element, so a line that starts with `>` or `!` also matches `extra_lines`. Every feedback or comment line can be read as choice text or as part of the previous feedback/comment line. Tested with Lark (Earley, explicit ambiguity), md_inline stubbed as a word or a run of spaces. Counter-examples (item content after the list marker): `[ ] Nile
> The Amazon
> it ahead
` has 4 parses: no feedback (both lines are choice text), feedback lines `The Amazon` and `it ahead`, one feedback `The Amazon > it ahead`, or text `Nile The Amazon` plus feedback `it ahead`. `[*] Lattes
> fb
! c1
! c2
` has 8 parses. The alternation `(feedback? comments? | comments feedback)` suggests two orders only, but `[ ] a
> f1
! c
> f2
` is accepted through extra_lines, with readings such as feedback `f1 ! c` + `f2` or comment `c > f2`. mdq-py reads it as feedback `f1 f2` and comment `c`, which no parse of the grammar produces.
data.impact: The grammar does not decide whether a `>` or `!` line is feedback, comment or choice text, nor whether feedback and comments can interleave. Implementations that follow the grammar can split the same item differently.
data.fix: Exclude lines whose first character is `>` or `!` from `extra_lines` (for example, `extra_line : (md_text_not_marker md_inline*)? nl`), and state in the prose whether interleaved feedback and comment lines are allowed and how they join.

data.title: feedback_line and comment_line accept continuation lines without the marker
data.snippet: feedback_line : ">" md_inline+ nl extra_lines?
data.description:
The prose (line 76) says feedback and comments span several lines, "each one preceded by their corresponding punctuation". The grammar appends `extra_lines?` to each `feedback_line` and `comment_line`, so a line without `>` or `!` continues the feedback. Counter-example: `[ ] b
> f1
lazy
` is accepted with feedback `f1 lazy`. mdq-py also reads feedback `f1 lazy`.
data.impact: The grammar and the prose disagree on whether a feedback or comment line may continue without its marker (lazy continuation, as in CommonMark block quotes).
data.fix: Either drop `extra_lines?` from `feedback_line` and `comment_line`, or change the prose to allow continuation lines without the marker.

data.title: choice_id does not encode the link lookahead that the prose requires
data.snippet: choice_id     : "[" SLUG "]"
data.description:
The prose (lines 56-59) says a bracket after the value is a choice id only when its content is a SLUG and the next character is not `(` or `[`. The grammar has no lookahead, and `md_inline+` can also start with the bracket. Counter-examples: `[ ] [rio](https://x) b
` has a parse with choice_id `rio` and text `(https://x) b`; `[ ] [rio][ref] text
` has a parse with choice_id `rio`; `[*] [Brasilia](https://x)
` (examples/valid/multiple-choice/link-choice.mdq.md) has a parse with choice_id `Brasilia`. In the other direction, `[*] [ipe-amarelo] Ipe
` has two parses: with choice_id `ipe-amarelo`, and with no id and text `[ipe-amarelo] Ipe`.
data.impact: The grammar alone accepts readings that the prose forbids, and does not say that a valid bracket is always the id. Only the prose settles it.
data.fix: Express the rule in the grammar, for example a terminal `CHOICE_ID : /\[[a-zA-Z0-9]+([-_][a-zA-Z0-9]+)*\](?![(\[])/` and a note that a match is always the choice id.

data.title: md_inline+ makes empty choice text a parse failure, but the rules treat it as blank-choice-text
data.snippet: item          : ws? "[" value "]" ws? (choice_id ws?)? md_inline+ nl extra_lines? (feedback? comments? | comments feedback)
data.description: The item requires `md_inline+` after the value and the optional id. The Additional Rules table (line 233) reports an empty text as `blank-choice-text`, which needs the item to parse. Counter-examples: `[*]\n` is rejected by the grammar, so the list is not a multiple-choice list; mdq-py reports `blank-choice-text`. `[ ] [rio]\n` parses only as text `[rio]` with no id, because the id leaves no text; the prose (next character is not `(` or `[`) makes `[rio]` a choice id, and mdq-py reports `blank-choice-text` for it.
data.impact: The grammar, the prose and the lint table give different results for a choice with no text: parse failure, text `[rio]`, or a choice id with blank text.
data.fix: Change `md_inline+` to `md_inline*` and leave empty text to the `blank-choice-text` rule, or state that the grammar rejects it and drop the lint.

data.title: An empty `>` or `!` line is choice text, not a blank feedback or comment
data.snippet: comment_line  : "!" md_inline+ nl extra_lines?
data.description:
`feedback_line` and `comment_line` require `md_inline+` after the marker. A line with only `>` or `!` therefore cannot be feedback or a comment; its only parse is a continuation of the choice text through `extra_lines`. Counter-examples: `[ ] a
>
` parses only with choice text `a >` and no feedback; `[ ] a
!
` parses only with choice text `a !`. The Additional Rules table (lines 236-237) has `blank-choice-feedback` and `blank-choice-comment`, which assume such a line is a feedback or comment with no visible character. mdq-py drops both lines and reports nothing.
data.impact: Three readings exist for the same input: grammar (choice text), lint table (blank feedback warning), mdq-py (ignored).
data.fix: Use `md_inline*` after the marker so that an empty line is a blank feedback or comment, which the lint codes then report.

data.title: The `!` comment marker collides with markdown image syntax
data.snippet: comment_line  : "!" md_inline+ nl extra_lines?
data.description: A continuation line that starts with an image, `![alt](src)`, matches `comment_line`. Counter-example: `[ ] c\n![Mapa](mapa.png)\n` has two parses: choice text with an image, or comment `[Mapa](mapa.png)`. The prose does not address it. mdq-py reads it as comment `Mapa`.
data.impact: An author cannot add an image on the next line of a choice: it silently becomes an instructor comment.
data.fix: Require a space or tab after `!` (`"!" ws md_inline*`), or state that a `!` followed by `[` is an image and not a comment.

data.title: percent accepts leading zeros, against the number convention of grammar.md
data.description: docs/references/grammar.md (line 69) says `INTEGER` and `DECIMAL` have no leading zeros and that the rules that use them add the sign. `percent` defines its own regex instead. Counter-examples accepted: `[050%]`, `[00.5%]`, `[-0%]`. mdq-py reads `[050%]` as 0.5.
data.impact: Number syntax is not uniform across the spec.
data.fix: Define `percent : /[+-]/? (DECIMAL | INTEGER) "%"`, or document that percentages allow leading zeros.

data.title: item requires a final line ending
data.snippet: item          : ws? "[" value "]" ws? (choice_id ws?)? md_inline+ nl extra_lines? (feedback? comments? | comments feedback)
data.description: Every item ends with `nl` (directly, or through `extra_lines`, `feedback_line` or `comment_line`). Counter-example: a file whose last line is `* [*] Brasília` with no final newline gives an UnexpectedEOF on the item content `[*] Brasília`. The prose does not forbid a missing final newline, and CommonMark accepts it.
data.impact: A literal reading of the grammar rejects the last choice of files without a trailing newline.
data.fix: End the item with `(nl | $END)`, or say that the item grammar applies to the item content with a line ending appended.

data.title: The grammar has no rule for the list, so indentation of feedback lines is undefined
data.snippet: Body consists of an unordered list of items. Each item follows the grammar:
data.description: Only `item` is defined; the list marker, the indentation of continuation lines and how it is removed are not. `feedback_line` has no `ws?` before `>`. Counter-example: `* [ ] a\n   > fb\n` (three spaces) leaves ` > fb` after the two-column list indentation is removed; the grammar parses it only as choice text, while CommonMark reads a block quote.
data.impact: Whether an over-indented `>` line is feedback depends on the implementation.
data.fix: Add a `list` rule (marker, continuation indentation), or allow `ws?` before `>` and `!`.

reason: duplicate of F4

data.description: The item requires `md_inline+` after the value and the optional id. The Additional Rules table (line 233) reports an empty text as `blank-choice-text`, which needs the item to parse. Counter-example: `[*]\n` (and `[*]` followed only by spaces, once markdown trims them) is rejected by the grammar, so the list is not a multiple-choice list at all; mdq-py parses it and reports `blank-choice-text`. The case of an item with only a choice id is F6.
data.impact: The grammar and the lint table give different results for a choice with no text: parse failure versus a `blank-choice-text` error on a parsed choice.

data.text: The `value` and `percent` rules of the multiple-choice item match the prose and the examples. Tested with Lark: accepted `[*]`, `[ ]`, `[\t]`, `[  ]`, `[ * ]`, `[ 50% ]`, `[100%]`, `[+50%]`, `[33.5%]`, `[-100%]`, `[150%]` (left to the schema range check, as the prose says); rejected `[]` (parse-error, as in examples/invalid/multiple-choice-empty-brackets), `[x]`, `[**]`, `[.5%]`, `[5.%]`, `[U+00A0]` and `[U+000B]`. Each of these accepted values has exactly one semantic parse.

The shared rules `ws`, `nl` and `SLUG` hold. `ws` accepts space, tab and mixes, and rejects U+00A0, U+3000, U+000B, U+000C and U+FEFF. `nl` accepts LF, CR and CRLF (CRLF as one line ending), and rejects U+000B, U+000C, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. `SLUG` accepts `Q1`, `ipe-amarelo`, `a_b`, `a-b_c` and `1`, and rejects `a--b`, `-a`, `a-`, `a_`, `ipê`, `a b`, `a.b` and the empty string, in Python `re` (Lark) and JavaScript `RegExp`. A U+00A0 before the item and in the value is rejected, and a U+2028 inside choice text stays text, as the prose of grammar.md requires.

`UNICODE_SPACE` matches exactly the 25 code points of the Unicode White_Space property (Python `str.isspace()` minus U+001C to U+001F) in Python `re`, and 25 code points in JavaScript `RegExp` with and without the `u` flag. `UNIT` excludes exactly `UNICODE_SPACE` plus `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`. The regex-dialect claims hold: JavaScript `\s` matches U+FEFF and not U+0085 or U+001C; Python `\s` matches U+0085 and U+001C and not U+FEFF.

data.description: The prose says each feedback or comment line is "preceded by their corresponding punctuation", but `feedback_line` and `comment_line` accept unmarked `extra_lines` after them. The `(feedback? comments? | comments feedback)` alternation suggests that interleaving (`> a`, `! b`, `> c`) is forbidden, but the prose never says so, no lint code covers it, and `extra_lines` absorbs the extra `>` line anyway (see the grammar finding on `extra_lines`). mdq-py accepts that item and joins the two feedback lines into `a c`.

data.title: Whitespace-only difference is a MAY in multiple-choice.md but a critical duplicate-choice-text error in lint-codes.md
data.snippet:
Implementations MAY reject choices that have different textual representations,
but that are visually identical when rendered to HTML.
data.description: multiple-choice.md presents `foo bar` vs `foo  bar` as an example of visually equivalent choices, which implementations MAY reject (info `visually-identical-choices` in the table). lint-codes.md defines `duplicate-choice-text` (critical) as "the same once whitespace is normalized outside code spans", which covers exactly that pair. mdq-py follows lint-codes.md: `* [*] [a] foo bar` / `* [ ] [b] foo  bar` fails with `duplicate-choice-text`. The multiple-choice text never says how texts are compared for the MUST-unique rule.
data.impact: Two implementations that follow different documents disagree on whether the document is valid (critical error vs optional info).
data.fix: State in multiple-choice.md, Choices, that uniqueness is checked after whitespace normalization outside code spans, and move the `a`/`b` pair out of the 'MAY reject' example (or use a different example of visual equivalence, such as `*foo*` vs `_foo_`).
data.conditions: Two choices that differ only in inline whitespace.

data.title: Additional Rules table lists rules that the multiple-choice text does not describe
data.snippet: | choices[].score    | info     | multiple-choice-no-correct-choice    | at least one choice should have a score of 1              |
data.description: The text has no statement for: at least two choices (`schema-error`), empty feedback string (`schema-error`), `blank-choice-feedback` and `blank-choice-comment` (warning), `multiple-choice-no-correct-choice` (info), `multiple-choice-many-correct-choices` (info; the text only says a question MAY mark any number of correct choices, which is a permission, not a lint) and `missing-choice-id` (info; the text only says the id is not mandatory). The text, in turn, says nothing about a question with zero correct choices.
data.impact: A reader of the prose cannot predict these diagnostics; the table is the only source.
data.fix: Add one sentence per rule to the Choices section (minimum of two choices, blank feedback/comment, zero correct choices, many correct choices, missing id), or mark them in the table as cross-type rules described elsewhere.

data.title: "MAY reject" and "MAY warn" map to info-level rules
data.snippet: is correct is unusual enough that implementations MAY warn about it.
data.description: The text says implementations MAY reject visually identical choices and MAY warn when every choice is correct. The table maps both to `info`, which by question-base.md produces a valid document. Rejecting is an error and 'warn' suggests the `warning` level, so the verbs do not match the levels.
data.impact: Readers can implement these as errors or warnings and still believe they follow the text.
data.fix: Reword as 'implementations MAY report it (info)' or similar, matching the table level.

data.title: No mapping from choice syntax to the AST fields
data.snippet:
Both the feedback and comments can span several lines, each one preceded by
their corresponding punctuation. Both are optional.
data.description: The document never states the AST shape of a choice (`text`, `id`, `score`, `feedback`, `comment`), how several `>` or `!` lines are joined into one string, how continuation lines of the choice text (`extra_lines`) are joined, or that the prose 'comments' becomes the singular field `comment`. The corpus (examples/valid/multiple-choice/comments.yaml) joins consecutive lines with a space, but the rule is only in a YAML comment of the example. multiple-selection.md, in contrast, shows its AST.
data.impact: Implementations can join lines with spaces or newlines and produce different documents from the same source.
data.fix: Add an AST subsection to Choices with a YAML example and the joining rule for text, feedback and comment lines.

data.title: "all-or-nothing" gives partial credit in multiple choice
data.snippet: * **all-or-nothing**: Unspecified scores are treated as 0[^2].
data.description: Since a declared score always wins, a choice marked `[50%]` scores 0.5 under `all-or-nothing` (examples/grading/multiple-choice.yaml confirms). In multiple-selection.md, `all-or-nothing` means any mistake gives zero. The strategy name promises a 0-or-1 result that multiple choice does not deliver, and an exam-wide `grading: all-or-nothing` behaves differently per type.
data.impact: An instructor who sets `all-or-nothing` on an exam to remove partial credit still gets fractional scores from multiple-choice questions.
data.fix: Decide whether all-or-nothing rounds non-1 scores to 0 for multiple choice, or document explicitly in Grading that declared fractional scores still count under all-or-nothing.

data.title: Symmetric strategy gives no explicit formula
data.snippet:
* **symmetric** (default): Unspecified scores are computed in such a way that
  the average score of randomly picking choices is zero.
data.description: The rule is stated only as a property (uniform random pick averages zero) plus a clamp. The intended value, `-(sum of declared scores) / (number of unspecified choices)` clamped to [-1, 0], must be derived from the table. 'Randomly picking' does not say the distribution is uniform over all choices, and after the clamp the average is no longer zero.
data.impact: Low: the table pins the cases, but an implementer has to reverse-engineer the formula.
data.fix: State the formula next to the property.

data.title: A multiple-choice list with no `*` or percent is inferred as multiple selection
data.snippet:
Multiple choice questions are represented by an unordered list with an ASCII-art
rendition of a radio button. Correct choices are marked with `[*]`.
data.description: By question-base.md Type inference, a list whose values are all blank is multiple selection. A multiple-choice question with no correct choice (allowed, info `multiple-choice-no-correct-choice`) therefore needs `type: multiple-choice`, as examples/valid/multiple-choice/no-correct-answer.mdq.md does. multiple-choice.md does not mention this.
data.impact: An author who writes such a question without `type` silently gets a multiple-selection question.
data.fix: Add a sentence that the type is inferred from `*` or a percentage, and that a list without them needs `type: multiple-choice`.

data.title: "Each choice carries a score" while a blank value omits it
data.snippet: Each choice carries a `score` on a scale from -1 to 1, derived from `value` in
data.description: The paragraph opens by saying every choice carries a score and ends by saying `[ ]` omits `score` from the document.
data.impact: Minor: readers may expect `score` to be required in the AST.
data.fix: Start with 'A choice may carry a `score`'.

data.title: Additional Rules lists the empty-string schema rule for feedback but not for comment
data.snippet: | choices[].feedback | critical | schema-error                         | must not be an empty string (schema)                      |
data.description: The schema sets `minLength: 1` on both `feedback` and `comment` (and `text`), but the table only has a `schema-error` row for `choices[].feedback`.
data.impact: Minimal: the table understates the schema.
data.fix: Add a `choices[].comment` row, or drop the feedback row since question-base.md already states the minLength rule for all text fields.

data.title: Only the `grading` description says null equals absent
data.snippet:
is `symmetric` outside an exam. A `null` value is the same as
          an absent field.

data.title: [Spec] Rewrite the multiple-choice item grammar to match the prose
data.summary: The `item` grammar is ambiguous (`extra_lines` absorbs `>` and `!` lines), lacks the link lookahead for `choice_id`, turns empty text and empty `>`/`!` lines into parse failures or choice text instead of the lint cases, requires a final newline, and does not define the list or its indentation. Recommended: one rewrite that (a) excludes marker lines from `extra_lines`, (b) uses a `CHOICE_ID` terminal with the `(`/`[` lookahead and says a match is always the id, (c) uses `md_inline*` for text, feedback and comment so the blank-* lints apply, (d) accepts end of input, (e) defines indentation or allows `ws?` before markers, (f) builds `percent` on `INTEGER`/`DECIMAL`. Alternative for (c): keep `+` and drop `blank-choice-text`, which loses the useful error message.
